mlb.hr_distance_tail_exceedance.assessment: Definition fits the 'per Statcast measurement' wording: a per-home-run tail of tracked projected distance, fitted per hitter with a park and temperature shift and an explicit shape sensitivity because observations beyond 500 ft are scarce. Weak points: coverage of hit_distance_sc for every home run and the contract's rounding at 500.0 are not verified; the input is market-free.

park altitude and orientation

mlb.bases_loaded_pa_opportunity.assessment: Separates the opportunity term (bases-loaded plate appearances by lineup slot and run environment) from the conversion term (grand slams per bases-loaded PA, shrunk with a 100-PA prior) so a 2+ grand-slam game is not priced as a scaled four-home-run game. Market-free; event files exist but the conversion prior and the independence of two PAs in one game are assumptions.
raw_data: plate-appearance events with base-out state, batter, lineup slot, result
team runs per game and lineup on-base rates
season-to-date and historical grand-slam counts per hitter

mlb.scoreless_streak_ledger_state.assessment: State variable of the survival product, kept under both run readings (all runs charged versus earned runs) because the contract text is silent; includes the post-game scoring-correction window. Market-free; feasibility rests on play-by-play carrying runs charged, earned flags and inherited-runner attribution, which is expected but not verified here, and on matching the exchange's own count.
raw_data: play-by-play: pitcher, outs, runs charged, earned flag, inherited runner flag
scoring changes after the game

mlb.leaguewide_rare_game_event_hazard.assessment: Definition is concrete (Poisson-rate regression on league K%, HR/PA and starter outs, with a generalised-Pareto tail for 500-ft drives and a bottom-up cross-check for multi-HR and grand-slam feats). Limitation: the single regression covers six very different events, and the 500-ft tail and grand-slam opportunity are better handled by the two dedicated inputs; counts are small integers so rate stability is an open empirical question (sstat_rate_stability).
raw_data: league-season counts of individual no-hitters, perfect games, 4+ HR games, 20+ K games, 2+ GS games, 500+ ft HR
league-season K%, HR per PA, starter outs per start
Statcast HR distances with park

mlb.any_pitcher_season_wins_threshold.assessment: Definition is concrete: Poisson-binomial per candidate from remaining starts and a per-start win probability built from the exit hazard and team lead-and-hold models, then a union across pitchers. Limitation: independence across pitchers and the lead-and-hold model are crude, and win credit depends on scoring rules (five-inning minimum) not stated in the contract.

start logs with outs recorded, score at exit and final decision

mlb.injuries_pit.assessment: Point-in-time injury status is sound and market-free; the main risk is timestamp leakage (using later IL backdating), which the as-of vintage requirement addresses. Generic across archetypes, so the per-archetype use (absorbing state for exposure, race eligibility) should be specified where it is attached.
